for_davis: Two threads to file: NVIDIA's open Nemotron 3.5 retrieval models are directly usable in your RAG project sprint, and the Fed/Challenger labor data sharpens the career pitch — you're aiming at the automation-building roles that survive the cuts. Keep the retake booking on top of the pile.
headline: DeepSeek's $15B raise, the Fed's AI labor data, and an open-model price war.

stories.summary: Two days after the US ordered federal civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek's AI technology over security concerns, the Hangzhou lab raised about $15B (~100B yuan), one of China's largest rounds, per Bloomberg. Potential investors include CATL and Tencent; DeepSeek is spending on infrastructure and open models for domestic and international markets. The raise follows a $7B+ round in June at a $50B valuation and a reported $1.5B raise at ~$71B in July, with a possible China IPO next year.
stories.title: DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US federal agencies were told to strip its tech
stories.why_it_matters: The open-model race is being funded at nation-state scale regardless of US policy — cheap, capable open models keep coming, which is what you'll build agents on.

stories.summary: The October Beige Book says firms in five of twelve Fed districts cut staffing through attrition, delayed hiring, or expect less job creation after AI productivity investments. Challenger, Gray & Christmas reports 120,136 planned US job cuts tied to AI through September — 21% of all cuts, the leading cited reason. Separately, Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in 'performance-based' layoffs from November to fund a pivot to AI inference accelerators, after a 20% YoY drop in handset revenue.
stories.title: The Fed's Beige Book: five of twelve districts report AI-linked staffing cuts or delayed hiring
stories.why_it_matters: Hard data on which roles are exposed first (routine dev and back-office) — and the flip side: money is flowing toward people who build and supervise automation.

stories.summary: Nvidia and Reflection released open models companies can run on their own servers — Ramp and EY are already tuning Nvidia's models for financial documents; Reflection launched with 40+ partners including AWS and Microsoft. DeepSeek and MiniMax cut prices again (MiniMax claims a 70% cost reduction); Inception says Mercury 3 answers 4-8x faster than rivals; Perplexity's new models make quick yes-or-no routing calls.
stories.title: Open-model price war: Nvidia and Reflection ship enterprise open weights, DeepSeek and MiniMax cut prices
stories.why_it_matters: Cheaper, faster, enterprise-ready open models lower the cost of every agent you build — and for your RAG project, tuned open weights are becoming a serious alternative to API calls.

stories.summary: NVIDIA released five open Nemotron 3.5 retrieval models (announced Oct 21): 8B and 1B embeds, an 8B reranker, and a 631M document parser — all openly available for commercial use. The company reports its reranker cut agentic token costs ~13-14% in selected tests while improving retrieval accuracy. They target the exact stack agents use to search internal knowledge bases before generating answers.
stories.title: NVIDIA ships open Nemotron 3.5 retrieval models: embed, rerank and parse for RAG
stories.why_it_matters: This is your S4 RAG sprint's toolkit: open embed/rerank/parse models you can self-host instead of paying per-query for retrieval.

stories.summary: Hugging Face (which Nvidia agreed to acquire for ~$13B in September) released Carbon-X, an open-source model combining DNA analysis/generation with plain language, built by training Qwen3-14B on genomic sequences from humans, mammals, plants and fungi with labs in Italy and China. A researcher can ask whether a mutation raises disease risk and get a prediction plus explanation — or generate new sequences for gene-therapy research.
stories.title: Hugging Face launches Carbon-X, an open model that lets scientists 'chat with DNA'
stories.why_it_matters: Open-weight science models keep advancing outside the big labs — relevant to your long-term health-tech angle, and another signal that frontier work isn't only closed models.

tldr: Geopolitics didn't slow the open-model race: DeepSeek raised a reported $15B two days after US agencies were told to strip its tech, while Nvidia and Reflection shipped enterprise open weights and Chinese labs cut prices again. The Fed's October Beige Book confirms AI-linked staffing cuts across five districts, and NVIDIA released open retrieval models aimed squarely at RAG.
